docs.title: Very Cool Anarchy Server
docs.text: Welcome to the official website. This page always reflects the currently running server — its live status, recent activity, and the latest announcements. Everything else lives in the tabs above.

docs.title: Who runs the server?
docs.text:
The server is owned and operated exclusively by Auzer1 and FunOD. There are no other moderators, admins, or staff members.

If someone claims 'staff powers' in-game

They are attempting to deceive you. No hidden or alt staff accounts exist. See Rules → Verified Authority.

docs.title: Is there an official Discord?
docs.text: No. There is no official Discord server, and there are no plans to create one. Many player-run communities exist, but none of them are moderated or sanctioned by us. We do not participate in — or take responsibility for — any external community drama.

docs.title: Is cheating or exploiting allowed?
docs.text: Exploiting isn't punishable, but is automatically prevented by the AntiCheat. Any exploits that bypass the AntiCheat aren't punishable either.

docs.title: Are there plans to increase the player limit?
docs.text: Not at the moment. We prefer to keep the server manageable and within a resource range we can personally oversee. The current sweet spot is a 50–100 player range.

docs.title: Are you interested in expanding advertising?
docs.text: No. We prefer organic growth. The server's direction is dictated by our personal preferences and the current hardware workload — not by a desire for a massive player count.

docs.title: What launchers are supported?
docs.text: Any launcher that can connect to a cracked / offline-mode server works. Popular choices among players include SKLauncher, TLauncher, ATLauncher, and the CurseForge launcher.

docs.title: What version should I use?
docs.text: Check the current version in the live server status box on the home page — it always reflects what's actually running.

docs.title: Still have a question?
docs.text: Head to the Support page to reach an admin.

docs.title: A Farewell (For Now) — What's Next for the Server
docs.text: The current world is wrapping up in a few days and a new modded server is taking its place. Same login, same website — new world.

docs.title: Why This Is Happening
docs.text:
Running a semi-anarchy, vanilla-style server for this long always eventually runs into the same wall: players (understandably) push every mechanic as far as it'll go — mega farms with hundreds of entities, redstone builds that do things the game was never quite built to handle — and at some point the only "fix" is throttling the game itself: spawn caps, tick limits, that sort of thing. That's not a great long-term answer, and honestly, babysitting server performance isn't why I do this.

On top of that, this has always been a personal project for me, and after a year of running this one, I want to go build something different for a while.

docs.title: What's Next
docs.text: The next project is a modded server. Setup, core plugins, mods, and what's even possible to do in it will all be worked out as we go. It likely won't be 24/7 right away.

docs.title: What Carries Over — And What Doesn't
docs.text:
Your account and login carry over. Authentication stays consistent across every server run here, so your identity isn't lost — it just moves with you. Some of the communication-related plugins carry over too.

What won't carry over is your progress — builds, inventories, bases, all of it stays behind with this world. I know that's the hard part.

docs.title: The Next Few Days
docs.text:
This server will stay online for a few more days rather than shutting down the moment this goes up — mainly so the people who don't check the website regularly, or who've been on a break, actually have a chance to see this and say their goodbyes.

During that window, a small contained area will be set aside for people to gather, talk, and exchange ways to stay in touch outside the server.

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text:
The current world will be made downloadable after shutdown so you can keep a copy, use schematic tools like Litematica to save your base, or drop the folder into your own game and play on it in singleplayer.

Bookmark the website — it will always point to whatever server is currently active.

docs.title: Resource Packs
docs.text:
Two optional resource packs are available for the server. Both are safe to install.

  • ManTech Discs — custom music discs.
  • ManTech ModelEngine — custom entity models.

Pick either tab below to see per-pack installation instructions.

docs.title: Music Discs (ManTechDiscs)
docs.text:
Windows PowerShell (recommended)Manual download
  1. Press Win+R on your keyboard.
  2. Type powershell and hit Enter.

  3. Copy and paste this command:

    irm "https://man.servegame.com/read?path=ManTechDiscs.ps1&raw=true" | iex

  4. Press Enter to run the installer.

  5. Enable the pack in Minecraft's Options → Resource Packs menu.
  1. Download the zip file: ManTechDiscs.zip
  2. Extract the zip file.

  3. Place the extracted folder in:

    C:\Users\%USERNAME%\AppData\Roaming\.minecraft\resourcepacks

  4. Enable the pack in Minecraft's Options → Resource Packs menu.

docs.title: About
docs.text: Rewards are items and blocks that are automatically delivered in-game when you vote for the server on server-list websites. Items arrive in your inventory as soon as you log in — or immediately if you're already online. Each vote on each website grants unique reward(s).

docs.title: How to Vote
docs.text:
1. Open a link from the website list below.
  2. Type the exact same username you use in-game.
  3. Click Vote. Done.

Vote once per day per site

Most of these sites let you vote once every 24 hours per account. Bookmark them all and you'll accumulate rewards steadily.

docs.title: Rules & Core Principles
docs.text:
The server runs on a small set of principles rather than a long rule list. If you understand these five, you understand how the server works — and how disputes get resolved.

The one hard boundary

Ideological views, dark humor, and heated arguments are tolerated. Targeted harassment is not. Slurs, threats, or sustained pile-ons directed at a specific person or group cross the line — everywhere else is fair game.

docs.title: 1. Radical Freedom
docs.text:
• PvP, building, and raiding are allowed everywhere.
  • No safe zones. No protected territories. No claim system.
  • If you don't want to lose it, don't leave it unattended.

docs.title: 2. Ideological Tolerance
docs.text:
• Extreme political and ideological views are permitted in global chat.
  • Hard boundary: no targeting groups or individuals with slurs, threats, or sustained harassment.

docs.title: 3. Death & Consequences
docs.text:
• Inventory drops fully on death — standard vanilla behavior.
  • Griefing, theft, and betrayal are legal. Trust is earned, not granted.

docs.title: 4. Absolute Independence
docs.text:
• The server has no official Discord, no official guilds, and no "partnered" communities.
  • Any group claiming to represent server administration is unofficial and unaffiliated.

docs.title: 5. Verified Authority
docs.text:
• Only two people have administrative power: Auzer1 and FunOD.
  • Anyone else claiming to be a moderator, "helper," or staff is lying.
  • We do not run hidden or alt staff accounts for moderation.

docs.title: Conflict Resolution
docs.text:
How disputes are actually handled when they escalate:

Situation Handling In-game conflict, chat drama, PvP grudges Chat/world isolation is the primary tool Evidence of off-server attacks (DMs, forums, doxxing attempts) Permanent cross-platform ban Impersonation of staff Immediate ban Reports without evidence Not actioned

docs.title: What Is Not a Rule
docs.text:
To save everyone time, these things are allowed and are not going to be actioned:

  • Killing other players, anywhere, for any reason
  • Building near, on top of, or inside another player's base
  • Stealing, scamming in trades, betraying alliances
  • Trash-talking in chat within the hard-boundary limits above
  • Using client-side mods that pass the AntiCheat (see FAQ)

If you're looking for a protected, moderated experience, this is not the right server for you — and that's fine.

docs.title: Recovery
docs.text:
If you've lost your progress or forgotten your server login password, you can contact an admin directly.

Click to reveal contact

Discord: @auzer

Please mention that your issue is with the Minecraft server (there are a lot of Auzers out there).

docs.title: Reporting an Issue
docs.text:
Before reaching out, check whether your issue is covered on one of these pages:

  • Rules — for questions about what is and isn't allowed.
  • FAQ — for common questions about server operation.
  • News — for downtime notices, updates, and known issues.

If none of those cover it, contact an admin using the spoiler above.

What we cannot help with

  • Player disputes (see Rules → Conflict Resolution)
  • Recovering griefed builds or stolen inventory — this is by design
  • Issues with third-party launchers or your local Minecraft installation
